1788.text: A wire mesh consisting of very small squares is viewed at a distance of $8 \mathrm{~cm}$ through a magnifying converging lens of focal length $10 \mathrm{~cm}$, kept close to the eye. The magnification produced by the lens is
1788.sol:
$u=-8 \mathrm{~cm}, f=10 \mathrm{~cm}$
As, $\frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f}$,

\therefore \quad $\frac{1}{v}=\frac{1}{f}+\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{10}+\frac{1}{-8}=\frac{1}{10}-\frac{1}{8}=\frac{4-5}{40}=\frac{-1}{40}$or, $v=-40 \mathrm{~cm}$.
Magnification produced by the lens, $m=\frac{v}{u}=\frac{-40}{-8}=5$.
This is a virtual image, erect and on the same side as the object.

5323.text: The mole fraction of a solute in one molal ethanolic solution would be
5323.sol:
1 molal solution means 1 mol of solute in 1000 g or $1 kg of ethanol.
Molecular weight of ethanol = 46.07 g/mol
Number of moles of ethanol
\begin{aligned} & \qquad=\frac{\text{ Weight of ethanol }}{\text{ Molecular weight of ethanol }} \\ & =\frac{1000 \mathrm{ g}}{46.07 \mathrm{ g} / \mathrm{mol}} \\ & =21.70 \mathrm{ mol} \\ & \therefore \text{ Mole fraction of solute }=\frac{1 \mathrm{ mol}}{1 \mathrm{ mol}+21.70 \mathrm{ mol}} \\ & =\frac{1 \mathrm{ mol}}{22.70 \mathrm{ mol}} \\ & =0.044\end{aligned}$
Hence, mole fraction of solute is 0.044.

8383.text: If \(y=$\sqrt{\frac{1+\tan x}{1-\tan x}}$\), then \($\frac{d y}{d x}=$\)
8383.sol:
Given, \$y=\sqrt{\frac{1+\tan x}{1-\tan x}}$
\begin{aligned}
\therefore \$quad\frac{d y}{d x}=$& $\frac{1}{2} \sqrt{\frac{1-\tan x}{1+\tan x}}\times \frac{(1-\tan x) \sec ^2 x+(1+\tan x) \sec ^2 x}{(1-\tan x)^2}$\\
= & $\frac{1}{2} \sqrt{\frac{1-\tan x}{1+\tan x}} \cdot \frac{2 \sec ^2 x}{(1-\tan x)^2}$\\
= & $\frac{1}{2} \sqrt{\frac{1-\tan x}{1+\tan x}} \frac{2}{(\cos x-\sin x)^2}$\\
= & $\frac{1}{2} \sqrt{\frac{1-\tan x}{1+\tan x}} \cdot \frac{1}{\left(\cos \left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\right)^2}$\\
= & $\frac{1}{2} \sqrt{\frac{1-\tan x}{1+\tan x}} \sec ^^2\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+$x\right)
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, option (a) is correct.

8535.text: If $4 x-3 y-5=0$ is a normal to the ellipse $3 x^2+8 y^2=k$, then the equation of the tangent drawn to this ellipse at the point $(-2, m)(m>0)$ is
8535.sol:
Given the equation of ellipse
$3 x^2+8 y^2=k\Rightarrow \frac{x^2}{\frac{k}{3}}+\frac{y^2}{\frac{k}{8}}=1$
Now, equation of normal to the ellipse at $\left(x_1, y_1\right)$ is $\frac{a^2}{x_1} x-\frac{b^2}{y_1} y=a^2-b^2\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{k}{38 x_1} x-\frac{k}{8 y_1} y=\frac{k}{3}-\frac{k}{8} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{x}{3 x_1}-\frac{y}{8 y_1}=\frac{5}{24} \Rightarrow \frac{8}{x_1} x-\frac{3}{y_1} y=5\end{aligned}$
Compare it with $4 x-3 y-5=0$
We get $\left(x_1, y_1\right)=(2,1)$
Now, $k=3 \times 4+8=20$ and $3 \times 4+8 m^2=20 \Rightarrow m=1, m>0$
Since, $3 x^2+8 y^2=20\Rightarrow 6 x+16 y y^{\prime}=0$ (Differentiate both side)
$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow y^{\prime}=\frac{-6 x}{16 y} \\ & \text{ at }(-2,1), y^{\prime}=\frac{12}{16}=\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}$
Now, equation of tangent at $(-2,1)$ is
$\begin{aligned}& y-1=\frac{3}{4}(x+2) \Rightarrow 4 y-4=3 x+6 \\
& \Rightarrow 3 x-4 y+10=0\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}
& P A^2+P B^2=2 P C^2 \\
& \begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow(x-2)^2+(y-3)^2+(x-3)^2+(y+6)^2 \\
=2\left[(x-5)^2+(y+7)^2\right]

& \begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow x^2+4-4 x+y^2+9-6 y+x^2+9-6 x \\
\quad+y^2+36+12 y
\end{aligned} \\
& =2\left[x^2+25-10 x+y^2+14 y+49\right] \\
& \Rightarrow 2 x^2+2 y^2-10 x+6 y+58 \\
& =2 x^2+2 y^2-20 x+28 y+148 \\
& \Rightarrow 10 x-22 y=90
\end{aligned}$
By checking options,
1. 10(2) − 22(− 5) = 20 + 110 =130
2. 10(− 2) − 22(5) = − 20 −110 = −130
3. 10(13) − 22(10) =130 − 220 = − 90
4. 10(−13) − 22(−10) = −130 + 220 = 90
So, point (− 13, − 10) lies on the locus of P

E_\mu & =-13.6 $\times \frac{207 m_e}{m_e} \mathrm{eV}$\\
& =-13.6 $\times207 \mathrm{eV}$
\end{aligned}$ \\ \left(\because$ m_\mu=207 m_e\right.$, where $m_e$ is the mass of electron $)$ \\ We know that \\ $r=$\frac{\varepsilon_0 h^2 n^2}{207 \pi m_{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{e}^2} \\ For ground state $(n-1)$ for proton, we have \\ $r_\mu=$\frac{\varepsilon_0 h^2}{207 \pi m_e \cdot e^2} \\ But \frac{\varepsilon_0 h^2}{\pi m_{\mathrm{e}} \cdot e^2}= ground state radius of hydrogen atom \\ \begin{aligned}$
$\frac{\varepsilon_0 h^2}{\pi m_e \cdot e^2}$& $=r_{\mathrm{H}$} \\
\therefore \quad r_\mu & =$\frac{r_{\mathrm{H}}}{207}$
\end{aligned}

15536.text: The length of a rod under longitudinal tension $T_1$ is $L_1$ and that under longitudinal tension $T_2$ is $L_2$. What is the actual length of the rod, in the absence of tensions?
15536.sol:
Let, the natural length of wire be $L_0$.
Using Hooke's law, Y=$\frac{T L_0}{A \Delta L}...($ i) where, $Y$ is Young's modulus of elasticity, $T$ is temperature, A$ is area and $\Delta L$ is change in length, i.e. $\Delta L=L-L_0 From $Eq. (i), we get L-L_0=\frac{T L_0}{A Y}$ Case 1 When tension is $T_1$ and length of wire $L=L_1$,
$L_1-L_0=\frac{T_1 L_0}{A Y}$...(ii)
Case 2 When tension is $T_2$ and length of wire $L=L_2L_2-L_0=\frac{T_2 L_0}{A Y}$...(iii)
Dividing Eq. (ii) by Eq. (iii), we get $\begin{aligned}& \frac{L_1-L_0}{L_2-L_0}=\frac{T_1}{T_2}\\
\Rightarrow \quad & L_0=\frac{L_1 T_2-L_2 T_1}{T_2-T_1}
\end{aligned}$

The ball is thrown vertically upwards then according to equation of motion (0)^2-u²=-2 g h and 0=u-g t From Eqs. (i) and (ii), h=$\frac{g t^2}{2}$ When the ball is falling downwards after reaching the maximum height $\begin{aligned} s & =u t^{\prime}+\frac{1}{2} g\left( t^{\prime}\right)^2 \\
\frac{h}{2}& =(0) t^{\prime}+\frac{1}{2} g\left( t^{\prime}\right)^2 \\
t^{\prime} & =\sqrt{\frac{h}{g}}\\
t^{\prime} & =\frac{t}{\sqrt{2}}
\end{aligned}$ Hence, the total time from the time of projection to reach a point at half of its maximum height while returning $=t+t^{\prime}$
=t+$\frac{t}{\sqrt{2}}$

18438.text: The locus of the point of intersection of two tangents to the parabola $y^{2}=4 a x,$ which are at right angle to one another is
18438.sol: Let the two tangents to the parabola \(y^{2}=4 a x\) be \(P T\) and \(Q T\) which are at right angle to one another at \($\mathrm{T}(\mathrm{h}, \mathrm{k})$\). Then we have a find the locus of \($\mathrm{T}(\mathrm{h}, \mathrm{k})$\). We know that \(y=m x+$\frac{a}{m}$\), where \(m\) is the slope is the equation of tangent to the parabola \(\mathrmy^{2}=4 $\mathrm{ax}$\) for all \($\mathrm{m}$\). Since this tangent to the parabola will pass through \($\mathrm{T}(\mathrm{h}, \mathrm{k})$\), so \($\mathrm{k}=\mathrm{mh}+\frac{\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{m}}$; $\text{ or } \mathrmm^{2} \mathrm{~h}-\mathrm{mk}+\mathrm{a}=$0\) This is a quadratic equation in \(m\), so will have two roots, say \(m_{1}\) and \(m_{2}\), then \($\mathrm{m}_{1}+\mathrm{m}_{2}=\frac{\mathrm{k}}{\mathrm{h}}$\), and \($\mathrm{m}_{1} \cdot \mathrm{m}_{2}=\frac{\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{h}}$\) Given that the two tangents intersect at right angle so \($\mathrm{m}_{1} \cdot \mathrm{m}_{2}=-$1 $\text{ or } \frac{\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{h}}=-$1 $\text{ or } \mathrm{h}+\mathrm{a}=$0\) The locus of \($\mathrm{T}(\mathrm{h}, \mathrm{k})$\) is \($\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{a}=$0\), which is the equation of directrix.

19489.subject: Chemistry
options: In the acid catalysed hydration of Ethene, an Oxonium ion is formed when it reacts with $\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{O}^{+}$ and a Carbocation is formed when the Oxonium ion reacts with water.
Cresols are less acidic than Phenol because electron releasing groups do not favour formation of Phenoxide ion.
Ethanol acts as Nucleophile when the $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$ bond is broken and acts as Electrophile on getting protonated.
In the reaction between Ethanol and Conc. $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ at 413 K , an Oxonium ion is formed when Ethanol gets protonated.
19489.sol:
In the acid catalysed hydration of ethene, the mechanism involves the protonation of ethene by $\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{O}^{+}$ to form a carbocation intermediate, not an oxonium ion. The water molecule then acts as a nucleophile to attack the carbocation. Thus, the statement in option (NCmIr) is incorrect.

Cresols contain a methyl group, which is an electron-donating group (+I effect). This destabilizes the phenoxide ion formed after the loss of a proton, making cresols less acidic than phenol. This statement is correct.

Ethanol acts as a nucleophile when the $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$ bond breaks (e.g., in esterification) and acts as an electrophile when the oxygen is protonated (e.g., in dehydration or substitution reactions where $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ is a leaving group). This statement is correct.

In the reaction between ethanol and concentrated $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4$ at 413 K, the first step is the protonation of the oxygen atom of ethanol to form an alkyloxonium ion, $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH}_2^{+}$. This statement is correct.

Answer: In the acid catalysed hydration of Ethene, an Oxonium ion is formed when it reacts with $\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{O}^{+}$ and a Carbocation is formed when the Oxonium ion reacts with water.

19490.text:
Identify $[\mathrm{X}]$ used in the given reaction.
$[\mathrm{X}]+$ Copper $/ 573 \mathrm{~K} \rightarrow[\mathrm{Y}] [\mathrm{Y}] \xrightarrow[\text{ (ii) } \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} / \mathrm{H}^{+}]{\text{(i) } \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{MgBr}}$ Tert.butyl alcohol. (major product)
19490.sol:
The reaction of $[\mathrm{Y}]$ with $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{MgBr}$ followed by hydrolysis yields tert-butyl alcohol, which is 2-methylpropan-2-ol. This indicates that $[\mathrm{Y}]$ must be acetone (propanone), as the Grignard reaction of acetone with methylmagnesium bromide produces tert-butyl alcohol.

The reaction $[\mathrm{X}] + \text{Copper} / 573 \mathrm{~K} \rightarrow [\mathrm{Y}]$ represents the dehydrogenation of an alcohol to a carbonyl compound. Since $[\mathrm{Y}]$ is propanone ($CH_3COCH_3$), $[\mathrm{X}]$ must be a secondary alcohol with three carbon atoms, which is propan-2-ol ($CH_3CH(OH)CH_3$).

The sequence is: Propan-2-ol $\xrightarrow{\text{Cu}, 573 \mathrm{K}}$ Propanone $\xrightarrow{\text{CH}_3\mathrm{MgBr}, \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}/\mathrm{H}^{+}}$ 2-methylpropan-2-ol.

Answer: Propan-2-ol

19915.subject: Chemistry
19915.text: Rate constant $(K)$ of a reaction has least value at
19915.sol:
The Arrhenius equation is given by $K = A e^{-E_{a} / (RT)}$, where $K$ is the rate constant, $A$ is the pre-exponential factor, $E_{a}$ is the activation energy, $R$ is the gas constant, and $T$ is the temperature in Kelvin.

To minimize the value of $K$, the exponent $-E_{a} / (RT)$ must be as small as possible (i.e., the most negative value).

This occurs when the magnitude of the exponent $E_{a} / (RT)$ is as large as possible. This requires $E_{a}$ to be high and $T$ to be low.

Therefore, the rate constant $K$ has the least value at low temperature $T$ and high activation energy $E_{a}$.

Answer: low $T$ and high $E_{a}$

20844.text:
The heat of combustion of carbon to $\text{CO}_2$ is -393.5 kJ $\text{mol}^{-1}$.
The heat released on the formation of 35.2 g of $\text{CO}_2$ by combustion of C is:

The combustion reaction of carbon is given by:

Molar mass of $\text{CO}_2 = 12 + 2 \times 16 = 44\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$

Number of moles of $\text{CO}_2$ formed $= \dfrac{35.2}{44} = 0.8\ \text{mol}$

Enthalpy change for the formation of $0.8\ \text{mol}$ of $\text{CO}_2 = 0.8 \times (-393.5\ \text{kJ}) = -314.8\ \text{kJ}$

Rounding to the nearest integer, the heat released (enthalpy change) is approximately $-315\ \text{kJ}$.

Answer: $-315\ \text{kJ}$

21038.text: The range of $x$ which satisfy the inequation : $-5 \leq \dfrac{2-3 x}{4} \leq 9$ is
21038.sol:
Given the inequality $-5 \leq \dfrac{2-3x}{4} \leq 9$.

Multiply all parts by $4$ to eliminate the denominator:

$-20 \leq 2-3x \leq 36$.

Subtract $2$ from all parts:

$-22 \leq -3x \leq 34$.

Divide by $-3$ and reverse the inequality signs:

$\dfrac{-22}{-3} \geq x \geq \dfrac{34}{-3}$.

Rearranging the terms gives:

$-\dfrac{34}{3} \leq x \leq \dfrac{22}{3}$.

Thus, the range of $x$ is $[-\dfrac{34}{3}, \dfrac{22}{3}]$.

Answer: $\left[-\dfrac{34}{3}, \dfrac{22}{3}\right]$

21328.text: The solution of the differential equation: $x \cos y d y=\left(x e^x \log x+e^x\right) d x$ is
21328.sol:
The given differential equation is $x \cos y \, dy = (x e^x \log x + e^x) \, dx$.

Rearranging the terms to separate the variables, we have $\cos y \, dy = \dfrac{x e^x \log x + e^x}{x} \, dx$.

Simplifying the right side, we get $\cos y \, dy = \left( e^x \log x + \dfrac{e^x}{x} \right) \, dx$.

Integrating both sides, $\int \cos y \, dy = \int (e^x \log x + \dfrac{e^x}{x}) \, dx$.

The integral of the right side can be solved by observing that $\dfrac{d}{dx}(e^x \log x) = e^x \log x + e^x \cdot \dfrac{1}{x}$.

Therefore, $\int (e^x \log x + \dfrac{e^x}{x}) \, dx = e^x \log x + c$.

The integral of the left side is $\sin y$.

Thus, $\sin y = e^x \log x + c$.

Answer: $\sin y=e^x \log x+c$

22356.subject: Physics
22356.text: If wattless current flows in an AC circuit, then the circuit is:
22356.sol:
The average power dissipated in an AC circuit is given by $P = V_{rms} I_{rms} \cos \phi$, where $\phi$ is the phase difference between the voltage and the current.

For wattless current, the average power dissipated must be zero, which means $P = 0$.

This implies $\cos \phi = 0$, so the phase difference $\phi = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ or $-\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

A phase difference of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ occurs only in purely inductive or purely capacitive circuits. In a purely capacitive circuit, the current leads the voltage by exactly $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, making the power factor zero.

Therefore, wattless current flows in a purely capacitive circuit.

Answer: Purely capacitive circuit

23180.subject: Physics
23180.text: A force $F$ applied on the wire of radius $r$ and length $L$ and change in the length of the wire is l. If the same force $F$ is applied on the wire of the same material and radius $4 r$ and length $4 l$, then change in length of the other wire is,
23180.sol:
Young's modulus $Y$ is defined as $Y = \dfrac{F L}{A l}$, where $A = \pi r^2$ is the cross-sectional area of the wire.

For the first wire, $Y = \dfrac{F L}{(\pi r^2) l}$.

For the second wire, let the change in length be $l'$. The material is the same, so $Y$ remains constant. The force is $F$, the radius is $4r$, and the length is $4L$.

$Y = \dfrac{F (4L)}{\pi (4r)^2 l'} = \dfrac{4 F L}{16 \pi r^2 l'} = \dfrac{F L}{4 \pi r^2 l'}$.

Equating the expressions for $Y$:

$\dfrac{F L}{\pi r^2 l} = \dfrac{F L}{4 \pi r^2 l'}$

$\dfrac{1}{l} = \dfrac{1}{4 l'}$

$l' = \dfrac{l}{4}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{l}{4}$

25336.text:
Let $z$ be a complex number satisfying ${\left|z\right|}^{3} + 2{z}^{2} + 4\overset{¯}{z} - 8 = 0$, where $\overset{¯}{z}$ denotes the complex conjugate of $z$. Let the imaginary part of $z$ be nonzero.

Match each entry in List-I to the correct entries in List-II.

List-I List-II
$\left(P\right)$ ${\left|z\right|}^{2}$ is equal to $\left(1\right)$ $12$
$\left(Q\right)$ ${\left|z - \overset{¯}{z}\right|}^{2}$ is equal to $\left(2\right)$ $4$
$\left(R\right)$ ${\left|z\right|}^{2} + {\left|z + \overset{¯}{z}\right|}^{2}$ is equal to $\left(3\right)$ $8$
$\left(S\right)$ ${\left|z + 1\right|}^{2}$ is equal to $\left(4\right)$ $10$
$\left(5\right)$ $7$

The correct option is
25336.sol:
Given,

${\left|z\right|}^{3} + 2{z}^{2} + 4\overset{¯}{z} - 8 = 0 . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Now on taking conjugate both side we get,

${\left|z\right|}^{3} + 2\overset{¯}{z}2 + 4z - 8 = 0 . . . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

$\left\{\text{Note}\left|\overset{¯}{z}\right| = \left|z\right|\right\}$

Now subtracting both equations we get,

$2\left({z}^{2} - \overset{¯}{z}2\right) + 4\left(\overset{¯}{z} - z\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(z - \overset{¯}{z}\right)\left[2\left(z + \overset{¯}{z}\right) - 4\right] = 0$

$∵ z = \overset{¯}{z}$ (not possible) or $4x = 4 ⇒ x = 1$ $\left\{\text{as}z + \overset{¯}{z} = 2x\right\}$

So, $z = 1 + \lambdai$

$⇒ \left|z\right| = \sqrt{1 + {\lambda}^{2}} \text{ and } \overset{¯}{z} = 1 - \lambdai$

Now putting the value of $z, \left|z\right| \text{ and } \overset{¯}{z}$ in given equation we get,

${\left(1 + {\lambda}^{2}\right)}^{3 / 2} + 2\left(1 - {\lambda}^{2} + 2\lambdai\right) + 4\left(1 - \lambdai\right) - 8 = 0$

$⇒ {\left(1 + {\lambda}^{2}\right)}^{3 / 2} + 2\left(1 - {\lambda}^{2}\right) = 4$

$⇒ {\left(1 + {\lambda}^{2}\right)}^{3 / 2} = 2\left(1 + {\lambda}^{2}\right)$

$⇒ \left(1 + {\lambda}^{2}\right)\left[\sqrt{1 + {\lambda}^{2}} - 2\right] = 0$

$⇒ {\lambda}^{2} = 3$

Now solving,

$\left(P\right)$ ${\left|z\right|}^{2} = 1 + {\lambda}^{2} = 1 + 3 = 4$

$\left(Q\right)$ ${\left|z - \overset{¯}{z}\right|}^{2} = {\left|1 + \lambdai - \left(1 - \lambdai\right)\right|}^{2} = {\left|2\lambdai\right|}^{2} = 4{\lambda}^{2} = 12$

$\left(R\right)$ ${\left|z\right|}^{2} + {\left|z + \overset{¯}{z}\right|}^{2} = 4 + {\left|\left(1 + \lambdai\right) + \left(1 - \lambdai\right)\right|}^{2} = 4 + 4 = 8$

$\left(S\right)$ ${\left|z + 1\right|}^{2} = {\left|1 + \lambdai + 1\right|}^{2} = 4 + {\lambda}^{2} = 4 + 3 = 7$

$∴ P \to \left(2\right), Q \to \left(1\right), R \to \left(3\right), S \to \left(5\right)$

26516.text: A glass beaker has a solid, plano-convex base of refractive index 1.60, as shown in the figure. The radius of curvature of the convex surface (SPU) is $9 \mathrm{~cm}$, while the planar surface (STU) acts as a mirror. This beaker is filled with a liquid of refractive index $n$ up to the level QPR. If the image of a point object $\mathrm{O}$ at a height of $h$ (OT in the figure) is formed onto itself, then, which of the following option(s) is(are) correct?
26516.sol: Since STU is a plane mirror, we can take mirror image of the whole situation about it and final image can be assumed to be at a distance $\mathrm{h}$ below the base. Since object and image are at same distance from equivalent lens, hence $\mathrm{h}=2 \mathrm{~F}_{\mathrm{eq}} \begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{\mathrm{~F}_{\mathrm{eq}}}=\left(\frac{1.6-1}{1}\right)\left(\frac{2}{9}\right)+\frac{(\mathrm{n}-1)}{1}\left(\frac{-2}{9}\right) \\ & \frac{1}{\frac{\mathrm{h}}{2}}=\frac{1.2}{9}+\frac{2(1-\mathrm{n})}{9} \\ & \frac{2}{\mathrm{~h}}=\frac{3.2-2 \mathrm{n}}{9} \\ & \mathrm{~h}=\frac{9}{1.6-\mathrm{n}} \mathrm{cm}\end{aligned}$ (1) for $\mathrm{n}=1.42, \mathrm{~h}=50 \mathrm{~cm}$ (2) for $\mathrm{n}=1.35, \mathrm{~h}=36 \mathrm{~cm}$ (3) for $\mathrm{n}=1.45, \mathrm{~h}=60 \mathrm{~cm}$ (4) for $\mathrm{n}=1.48, \mathrm{~h}=75 \mathrm{~cm}$

26560.text: A biconvex lens of focal length $15 \mathrm{~cm}$ is in front of a plane mirror. The distance between the lens and the mirror is 10 $\mathrm{cm}$. A small object is kept at a distance of $30 \mathrm{~cm}$ from the lens. The final image is
options:
virtual and at a distance of $16 \mathrm{~cm}$ from the mirror

real and at a distance of $16 \mathrm{~cm}$ from the mirror

virtual and at a distance of $20 \mathrm{~cm}$ from the mirror

real and at a distance of $20 \mathrm{~cm}$ from the mirror
26560.sol:
Object is placed at distance $2 f$ from the lens. So first image $I_1$ will be formed at distance $2 f$ on other side. This image $I_1$ will behave like a virtual object for mirror. The second image $I_2$ will be formed at distance $20 \mathrm{~cm}$ in front of the mirror, or at distance $10 \mathrm{~cm}$ to the left hand side of the lens.
Now applying lens formula $\begin{array}{rlr}$& $\frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f}$\\ & $\frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{+10}=\frac{1}{+15}$\\ $\text{ or }$& v=6 $\mathrm{~cm} \end{array}$Therefore, the final image is at distance $16 \mathrm{~cm}$ from the mirror. But, this image will be real. This is because ray of light is travelling from right to left. $\therefore$ The correct option is (b).

27187.subject: Chemistry
27187.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: Heating benzamide with bromine in an ethanolic solution of sodium hydroxide will give benzylamine.
Statement II: Nitration of aniline with $HNO_3/H_2SO_4$ at $288\text{ K}$ produces $m$-nitroaniline in higher amount than $o$-nitroaniline (pH adjusted).
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
27187.sol:
Statement I describes the Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction. When benzamide ($C_6H_5CONH_2$) is heated with bromine in an ethanolic solution of sodium hydroxide, it produces aniline ($C_6H_5NH_2$), not benzylamine. Thus, Statement I is false.

Statement II describes the nitration of aniline. Direct nitration of aniline with $HNO_3/H_2SO_4$ yields a mixture of $p$-nitroaniline ($51\%$), $m$-nitroaniline ($47\%$), and $o$-nitroaniline ($2\%$). The significant formation of the meta derivative is due to the protonation of aniline in the strongly acidic medium to form the anilinium ion, which is meta-directing. Since $47\% > 2\%$, $m$-nitroaniline is produced in a higher amount than $o$-nitroaniline. Thus, Statement II is true.

Answer: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

29292.subject: Chemistry
29292.text:
Molar conductivity of a weak acid HQ of concentration 0.18 M was found to be $1 / 30$ of the molar conductivity of another weak acid HZ with concentration of 0.02 M. If $\lambda^{\circ} \mathrm{Q}^{-}$happened to be equal with $\lambda^{\circ} \mathrm{Z}^{-}$, then the difference of the $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}$ values of the two weak acids $\left(\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}(\mathrm{HQ})-\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}(\mathrm{HZ})\right)$ is $\_\_\_\_$ (Nearest integer).
[Given: degree of dissociation $(\alpha) \ll 1$ for both weak acids, $\lambda^{\circ}$ : limiting molar conductivity of ions]
29292.sol:
For weak acids with $\lambda^{\infty}Q^- = \lambda^{\infty}Z^-$, the molar conductivity is $\lambda_m = \alpha \lambda^{\infty}$.
From $\lambda_m^Q = \frac{1}{30}\lambda_m^Z$, we get $\alpha_Q = \frac{\alpha_Z}{30}$.
Using $K_a = \alpha^2 C$ for weak acids: $K_a(HQ) = \alpha_Q^2 \times 0.18 = \frac{\alpha_Z^2 \times 0.18}{900}$ and $K_a(HZ) = \alpha_Z^2 \times 0.02$.
Therefore $\frac{K_a(HZ)}{K_a(HQ)} = \frac{0.02 \times 900}{0.18} = 100$.
Thus $pK_a(HQ) - pK_a(HZ) = \log(100) = 2$.

29838.sol:
Compound A is optically active due to the presence of chiral carbon

The R / S system is an important nomenclature system for denoting enantiomers. This approach labels each chiral center R or S according to a system by which its substituents are each assigned a priority, according to the Cahn–Ingold–Prelog priority rules (CIP), based on atomic number. When the center is oriented so that the lowest-priority substituent of the four is pointed away from the viewer, the viewer will then see two possibilities: if the priority of the remaining three substituents decreases in clockwise direction, it is labeled R (for Rectus, Latin for right); if it decreases in counterclockwise direction, it is S (for Sinister, Latin for left)

But the absolute configuration of both the molecules A and B is same that is S

Hence, Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

$solute n = solvent n = \dfrac{100}{18} = 5 . 55mol$

33791.text: Let $P = \left\{z \in \mathbb{C}: \left|z + 2 - 3i\right| \le 1\right\}$ and $Q = \left\{z \in \mathbb{C}: z\left(1 + i\right) + \overset{¯}{z}\left(1 - i\right) \le - 8\right\}$. Let in $P ∩ Q, \left|z - 3 + 2i\right|$ be maximum and minimum at ${z}_{1}$ and ${z}_{2}$ respectively. If ${\left|{z}_{1}\right|}^{2} + 2{\left|z\right|}^{2} = \alpha + \beta\sqrt{2},$ where $\alpha, \beta$ are integers, then $\alpha + \beta$ equals __________
33791.sol:
Given: $\left|z + 2 - 3i\right| \le 1$

Putting, $z = x + iy$.

$⇒ {\left(x + 2\right)}^{2} + {\left(y - 3\right)}^{2} \le 1 . . . \left(i\right)$

For the circle represented in equation $\left(i\right)$, centre is $\left(- 2, 3\right)$ and radius, $r = 1$.

It is given that, $z\left(1 + i\right) + z \left(1 - i\right) \le - 8$

$⇒ \left(x + iy\right)\left(1 + i\right) + \left(x - iy\right)\left(1 - i\right) \le - 8$

$⇒ x + ix - y + iy + x - ix - iy - y \le - 8$

$⇒ 2x - 2y \le - 8$

$⇒ x - y + 4 = 0$

So, the line passing through $\left(3, - 2\right)$ and perpendicular to $x - y + 4 = 0$ is given by, $x + y - 1 = 0$.

So, the distance of line $x - y + 4 = 0$ from the centre $\left(- 2, 3\right)$ is given by,

$d = \left|\dfrac{- 2 - 3 + 4}{\sqrt{2}}\right|$

$⇒ d = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Now, $x + y - 1 = 0$ can be rewritten as,

$\dfrac{x + 2}{\dfrac{- 1}{\sqrt{2}}} = \dfrac{y - 3}{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}} = CA\text{or}CB$

For $CA = \dfrac{- 1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $CB = 1$, $A ≡ \left(\dfrac{- 3}{2}, \dfrac{5}{2}\right)$ and $B ≡ \left(\dfrac{- 1}{\sqrt{2}} - 2, \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + 3\right)$.

$⇒ {\left|{z}_{1}\right|}^{2} = {\left(2 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}^{2} + {\left(3 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ {\left|{z}_{1}\right|}^{2} = 4 + \dfrac{1}{2} + 2\sqrt{2} + 9 + \dfrac{1}{2} + 3\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ {\left|{z}_{1}\right|}^{2} = 14 + 5\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ {\left|{z}_{2}\right|}^{2} = 2\left(\dfrac{9}{4} + \dfrac{25}{4}\right)$

$⇒ {\left|{z}_{2}\right|}^{2} = 17$

$⇒ {\left|{z}_{1}\right|}^{2} + 2{\left|{z}_{2}\right|}^{2} = 31 + 5\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ \alpha = 31, \beta = 5$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta = 36$

34120.subject: Mathematics
34120.sol:
Given integral is $I = \displaystyle\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/4}\left(\cot\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\cot\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)+1\right)dx$

Using the identity $\cot A \cot B + 1 = \dfrac{\cos(A-B)}{\sin A \sin B}$, the integrand simplifies to:

$f(x) = \dfrac{\cos\left(\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) - \left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\right)}{\sin\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\sin\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)}$

$f(x) = \dfrac{\cos\left(-\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)}{\sin^2 x - \sin^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)}$

$f(x) = \dfrac{-1/2}{\sin^2 x - 3/4} = \dfrac{2}{3 - 4\sin^2 x}$

Dividing the numerator and the denominator by $\cos^2 x$:

$f(x) = \dfrac{2\sec^2 x}{3\sec^2 x - 4\tan^2 x} = \dfrac{2\sec^2 x}{3(1+\tan^2 x) - 4\tan^2 x} = \dfrac{2\sec^2 x}{3 - \tan^2 x}$

The integral becomes:

$I = \displaystyle\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/4} \dfrac{2\sec^2 x}{3 - \tan^2 x} dx$

Substituting $\tan x = t \Rightarrow \sec^2 x dx = dt$.

When $x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$, $t = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$. When $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, $t = 1$.

$I = \displaystyle\int_{1/\sqrt{3}}^{1} \dfrac{2}{3 - t^2} dt$

Using the standard integral $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{1}{a^2 - x^2} dx = \dfrac{1}{2a}\ln\left|\dfrac{a+x}{a-x}\right|$:

$I = 2 \left[ \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{3}} \ln\left|\dfrac{\sqrt{3}+t}{\sqrt{3}-t}\right| \right]_{1/\sqrt{3}}^{1}$

$I = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \left( \ln\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}+1}{\sqrt{3}-1}\right) - \ln\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}{\sqrt{3}-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}\right) \right)$

$I = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \left( \ln\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}+1}{\sqrt{3}-1}\right) - \ln\left(\dfrac{3+1}{3-1}\right) \right)$

$I = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \left( \ln\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}+1}{\sqrt{3}-1}\right) - \ln 2 \right) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \ln\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2(\sqrt{3}-1)}\right)$

Rationalizing the term inside the logarithm by multiplying the numerator and the denominator by $(\sqrt{3}-1)$:

$\dfrac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2(\sqrt{3}-1)} = \dfrac{(\sqrt{3}+1)(\sqrt{3}-1)}{2(\sqrt{3}-1)^2} = \dfrac{3-1}{2(\sqrt{3}-1)^2} = \dfrac{1}{(\sqrt{3}-1)^2} = (\sqrt{3}-1)^{-2}$

Thus,

$I = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \ln\left((\sqrt{3}-1)^{-2}\right) = -\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \ln(\sqrt{3}-1)$

Comparing this with $I = \alpha\log_e(\sqrt{3}-1)$, we get:

$\alpha = -\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$

Therefore, $9\alpha^2 = 9 \left(-\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^2 = 9 \times \dfrac{4}{3} = 12$.

Answer: $12$

34218.text: Let $[ t ]$ denote the greatest integer $\le t$. Then $\dfrac{2}{\pi}{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{5\pi}{6}}\left(8\left[cosecx\right] - 5\left[cotx\right]\right)dx$ is equal to $_______$
34218.sol:
Let,

$I = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{5\pi}{6}}\left(8\left[cosecx\right] - 5\left[cotx\right]\right)dx$

$⇒ I = 8{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{5\pi}{6}}\left[cosecx\right]dx - 5{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{5\pi}{6}}\left[cotx\right]dx$

$⇒ I = 8{I}_{1} - 5{I}_{2}$, where ${I}_{1} = 8{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{5\pi}{6}}\left[cosecx\right]dx \text{$ and $} {I}_{2} = 5{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{5\pi}{6}}\left[cotx\right]dx$

Now solving,

${I}_{1} = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{5\pi}{6}}\left[cosecx\right]dx$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{5\pi}{6}}1dx = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

As when $x \in \left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}, \dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right), cosecx \in [ 1, 2 )$,

So, $\left[cosecx\right] = 1$

Now solving,

${I}_{2} = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{5\pi}{6}}\left[cotx\right]dx$

$⇒ {I}_{2} = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}1dx + {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{4}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}0dx + {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\dfrac{3\pi}{4}}\left(- 1\right)dx + {∫}_{\dfrac{3\pi}{4}}^{\dfrac{5\pi}{6}}\left(- 2\right)dx$

$⇒ {I}_{2} = \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) - \left(\dfrac{3\pi}{4} - \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - 2\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6} - \dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right)$

$⇒ {I}_{2} = - \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

Required value will be,

$\dfrac{2}{\pi}I = \dfrac{2}{\pi}\left[8 \times \dfrac{2\pi}{3} + 5 \times \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right] = 14$

34385.sol:
$f\left(2 - x\right) = f\left(2 + x\right)$ and $f\left(4 - x\right) = f ( 4 + x )$

Then curve is symmetric about $x = 2$ and $x = 4$

$∴$ The curve is periodic with period $4$

Given $\mathop{∫}_{0}^{2}f\left(x\right)dx = 5$

$\mathop{∫}_{0}^{4}f\left(x\right)dx = 2\mathop{∫}_{0}^{2}f\left(x\right)dx = 10$

$\mathop{∫}_{10}^{50}f\left(x\right)dx = \mathop{∫}_{2\left(4\right) + 2}^{12\left(4\right) + 2}f\left(x\right)dx$

$= \left(12 - 2\right)\mathop{∫}_{0}^{4}f\left(x\right)dx$

$= 10 \times 10 = 100$

If $e$ is eccentricity of the hyperbola, then ${e}^{2} = 1 + \dfrac{{b}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}$

$1 + \dfrac{{b}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} = \dfrac{5}{2}$$⇒ {b}^{2} = \dfrac{3{a}^{2}}{2}$

Length of the latus-rectum is given by $\dfrac{2{b}^{2}}{a}$

i.e. $\dfrac{2{b}^{2}}{a} = 6\sqrt{2}$

$\dfrac{2}{a} \times \dfrac{3{a}^{2}}{2} = 6\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ a = 2\sqrt{2}$

and ${b}^{2} = \dfrac{3}{2} \times 8 = 12$

$⇒ b = 2\sqrt{3}$

If $y = mx + c$ is a tangent to the hyperbola, then ${c}^{2} = {a}^{2}{m}^{2} - {b}^{2}$

$∴ {c}^{2} = 4 \times 8 - 12$

Hence ${c}^{2} = 20$

35467.text: Let $\mathrm{P}(3 \sec \theta, 2 \tan \theta)$ and $\mathrm{Q}(3 \sec \phi, 2 \tan \phi)$ where $\theta+\phi=\frac{\pi}{2}$, be two distinct points on the hyperbola $\frac{x^2}{9}-\frac{y^2}{4}=1$. Then the ordinate of the point of intersection of the normals at $\mathrm{P}$ and $\mathrm{Q}$ is:
35467.sol:
Let the coordinate at point of intersection of normals at $\mathrm{P}$ and $\mathrm{Q}$ be $(h, k)$ Since, equation of normals to the hyperbola $\frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ At point $\left(x_1, y_1\right)$ is $\frac{a^2 x}{x_1}+\frac{b^2 y}{y_1}=a^2+b^2$ therefore equation of normal to the hyperbola $\frac{x^2}{3_1^2}-\frac{y^2}{2^2}=1$ at point $P(3 \sec \theta, 2 \tan \theta)$ is

$\begin{aligned}$&$\frac{3^2 x}{3 \sec \theta}+\frac{2^2 y}{2 \tan \theta}=$3^2+2^2 \\
&\Rightarrow 3 x \cos $\theta+$2 y \cot $\theta=$3^2+2^2
\end{aligned}

Similarly, Equation$ of normal to the hyperbola\frac{x^2}{3^2}-\frac{y^2}{2^2}$ at point Q $(3 \sec \phi, 2 \tan \phi)$ is

$\begin{aligned}$&$\frac{3^2 x}{3 \sec \phi}+\frac{2^2 y}{2 \tan \phi}=$3^2+2^2 \\
&\Rightarrow 3 x \cos \phi+2 y \cot \phi=3^2+2^2
\end{aligned}

Given $\theta+\phi=\frac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow \phi=\frac{\pi}{2}-\theta$ and these passes through $(h, k)\therefore$ From eq. (2)

$\begin{aligned}$&3 x \cos $\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\theta\right)+$2 y \cot $\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\theta\right)=$3^2+2^2 \\
&\Rightarrow 3 h \sin $\theta+$2 k \tan $\theta=$3^2+2^2
\end{aligned}$ and 3 h \cos \theta+2 k \cot \theta=3^2+2^2$
Comparing equation (3) \& (4), we get
$3 h \cos \theta+2 k \cot \theta=3 h \sin \theta+2 k \tan \theta3 h \cos \theta-3 h \sin \theta=2 k \tan \theta-2 k \cot \theta3 h(\cos \theta-\sin \theta)=2 k(\tan \theta-\cot \theta)3 h(\cos \theta-\sin \theta)=2 k \frac{(\sin \theta-\cos \theta)(\sin \theta+\cos \theta)}{\sin \theta \cos \theta}$
or, $3 \mathrm{~h}=\frac{-2 k(\sin \theta+\cos \theta)}{\sin \theta \cos \theta}$
Now, putting the value of equation (5) in eq. (3)

$\begin{aligned}$&$\frac{-2 k(\sin \theta+\cos \theta) \sin \theta}{\sin \theta \cos \theta}+$2 k \tan $\theta=$3^2+2^2 \\
&\Rightarrow 2 k \tan $\theta-$2 k+2 k \tan $\theta=$13 \\
&-2 k=13 \Rightarrow k=$\frac{-13}{2}
\end{aligned}$Hence, ordinate of point of intersection
of normals at $P and Q$ is $\frac{-13}{2}$

35944.subject: Mathematics
35944.text:
Consider :
Statement - $I$ : $\left(p ∧ ~ q\right) ∧ \left(~ p ∧ q\right) is a fallacy.
Statement - $II$ : \left(p \to q\right) ↔ \left(~ q \to ~ p\right) is a tautology.$
options: Statement - $I$ is true; statement - $II$ is false.
Statement - $I$ is false; Statement -$II$ is true.
Statement - $I$ true; Statement -$II$ is true; Statement -$II$ is a correct explanation for Statement - $I$.
Statement - $I$ is true; Statement - $II$ is true; Statement - $II$ is not a correct explanation for Statement - $I$.
35944.sol:
The truth table for Statement $I$ is

$p$ $q$ $~ p$ $~ q$ $p ∧ ~ q$ $~ p ∧ q$ $\left(p ∧ ~ q\right) ∧ \left(~ p ∧ q\right)

$TTFF$

 $TFTF$ $FFTT$ $FTFT$ $FTFF$ $FFTF$

$FFFF$

Hence, it is a fallacy.

The truth table for statement $II$ is

$p$ $q$ $~ p$ $~ q$ $p \to q$ $~ q \to ~ p$ \left(p \to q\right) ↔ \left(~ q \to ~ p\right)
$TTFF$ $TFTF$ $FFTT$ $FTFT$ $TFTT$ $TFTT$ $TTTT

Hence, it is a tautology.

But, the second statement is not a correct explanation for the first.

36265.text: A tangent is drawn to the parabola ${y}^{2} = 6x$ which is perpendicular to the line $2x + y = 1$. Which of the following points does NOT lie on it?
36265.sol:
Slope of tangent $= {m}_{T} = m$

So, $m\left(- 2\right) = - 1 ⇒ m = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Equation: $y = mx + \dfrac{a}{m}$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{1}{2}x + \dfrac{3}{2 \times \dfrac{1}{2}}\left(∵ a = \dfrac{6}{4} = \dfrac{3}{2}\right)$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{x}{2} + 3$

$⇒ 2y = x + 6$

Point $\left(5, 4\right)$ will not lie on it

37438.text: The minimum number of elements that must be added to the relation $R = ( a, b ) , ( b, c )$ on the set ${ a, b, c }$ so that it becomes symmetric and transitive is:
37438.sol:
Given:

A = $\left\{a, b, c, d\right\}$

And,

$R = \left\{\left(a, b\right)$, $\left(b, c\right)$\right\}$

For symmetric relation, we must add \left(b, a\right), \left(c, b\right).

So, $R = $\left\{\left(a, b\right), \left(b, a\right)$, $\left(b, c\right)$, $\left(c, b\right)$\right\}$.

For transitive relation, we must add

\left(a, c\right), \left(b, b\right), \left(c, a\right)$, $\left(a, a\right)$, $\left(c, c\right)$

Hence,

$R = \left\{\left(b, a\right)$, $\left(c, b\right)$, $\left(a, c\right), \left(b, b\right), \left(c, a\right), \left(a, a\right), \left(c, c\right)$, $\left(a, b\right)$, $\left(b, c\right)\right\}$

So, number of new elements added$= 7$

An angle between the plane, $x+y+z=5$ and the line of intersection of the planes, $3 x+4 y+z-1$ $=0$ and
$5 x+8 y+2 z+14=0$, is
38211.sol:
Normal to $3 x+4 y+z=1$ is $3 \hat{i}+4 \hat{j}+k$.
Normal to $5 x+8 y+2 z=-14$ is $5 \hat{i}+8 \hat{j}+2 \hat{k}$
The line of intersection of the planes is perpendicular to both normals, so, direction ratios of the intersection line are directly proportional to the cross product of the normal vectors.
Therefore the direction ratios of the line is $-\hat{j}+4 \hat{k}$
Hence the angle between the plane $x+y+z+5=0$ and the intersection line is $\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{-1+4}{\sqrt{17} \sqrt{3}}\right)=\sin ^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\frac{3}{17}}\right)$

$\overset{\to}{G} = \dfrac{2\overset{\to}{C} + \overset{\to}{R}}{3}$

$3\overset{\to}{G} = 2\overset{\to}{C} + \overset{\to}{R}$

$\overset{\to}{R} = 3\overset{\to}{G} - 2\overset{\to}{C} = ( \overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c} ) - 2\left(\dfrac{\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c}}{4}\right)$

$=\dfrac{\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c}}{2}$

39376.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
39376.text: Distance of the centre of mass of a solid uniform cone from its vertex is ${z}_{0}$. If the radius of its base is $R$ and its height is $h$ then ${z}_{0}$ is equal to:
39376.sol:
Let the mass of solid cylinder is $M$ and angle with vertical is $\theta$. Now, we take a small element of thickness $d y$ at a distance $y$ from the vertex. The radius of small element is $r$, as shown in the figure below.

Then, $tan \theta = \dfrac{R}{h} = \dfrac{r}{y}$ which will give, $r = ytan \theta$. The density of the cone is given by,

$ρ = \dfrac{M}{\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\pi{R}^{2}h} = \dfrac{3M}{\pi{R}^{2}h}$.

The mass of the small element is given by,

$d M = ρ d V$

$d M = \dfrac{3M}{\pi{R}^{2}h} \times \pi{r}^{2} d y = \dfrac{3M{y}^{2}\tan^{2}\theta}{{R}^{2}h} d y$

The center of mass of the cone is given by,

${z}_{0} = \dfrac{1}{M}{∫}_{0}^{h}y d M$

${z}_{0} = \dfrac{1}{M}{∫}_{0}^{h}y \cdot \dfrac{3M{y}^{2}\tan^{2}\theta}{{R}^{2}h} d y$

${z}_{0} = \dfrac{3}{{R}^{2}h}{\left(\dfrac{R}{h}\right)}^{2}{\left[\dfrac{{y}^{4}}{4}\right]}_{0}^{h}$

${z}_{0} = \dfrac{3h}{4}$.

$⇒ {q}_{en} = {E}_{0}{ε}_{0}{a}^{3}$

$= 4 \times {10}^{4} \times 9 \times {10}^{- 12} \times 8 \times {10}^{- 6}$

$= 288 \times {10}^{- 14}C$

Hence, the value of $Q = 288$.

41690.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I : The diamagnetic property depends on temperature.

Statement II : The induced magnetic dipole moment in a diamagnetic sample is always opposite to the magnetising field.

In the light of given statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are False
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
41690.sol:
The properties of a diamagnetic material are as follows:

1. The susceptibility has a low negative value.

2. Susceptibility is independent of temperature.

43812.subject: Physics
43812.text: An ideal gas at pressure $P$ and temperature $T$ is expanding such that $PT^3 = $ constant. The coefficient of volume expansion of the gas is _______.
43812.sol:
Given the process equation for the ideal gas:

$PT^3 = \text{constant}$

From the ideal gas equation, $PV = nRT$, which gives $P = \dfrac{nRT}{V}$.

Substituting $P$ into the process equation:

$\left(\dfrac{nRT}{V}\right) T^3 = \text{constant}$

$\dfrac{T^4}{V} = \text{constant}$

$V = k T^4$

Differentiating both sides with respect to temperature $T$:

$\dfrac{dV}{dT} = 4k T^3$

The coefficient of volume expansion $\gamma$ is defined as:

$\gamma = \dfrac{1}{V} \dfrac{dV}{dT}$

Substituting the values of $V and \dfrac{dV}{dT}$:

$\gamma = \dfrac{1}{k T^4} (4k T^3) = \dfrac{4}{T}$

Answer: $\dfrac{4}{T}$

Emf of second cell is $1.67$

55296.subject: Chemistry
55296.text: Which from following is a correct decreasing order of water solubilities of organic compounds?
55296.sol:
Decreasing order of water solubility: Alcohols > Amines > Alkanes

Water solubility depends on the ability to form hydrogen bonds. Alcohols contain a polar O-H group, forming strong hydrogen bonds with water due to oxygen's high electronegativity (O \approx 3.44$). Amines with N-H groups form moderately strong hydrogen bonds, though nitrogen's lower electronegativity (N \approx 3.04$) results in weaker bonding than alcohols. Alkanes are nonpolar and cannot form hydrogen bonds, exhibiting only London dispersion forces.

56353.subject: Chemistry
56353.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
56353.text: Which group elements have the smallest atomic radii in their respective periods?
56353.sol:
In a given period, the atomic radius decreases from left to right as the effective nuclear charge increases.

This trend continues up to group 17 (halogens).

For group 18 (noble gases), the atomic radius is expressed as van der Waals radius since they do not form covalent bonds under normal conditions.

Since van der Waals radii are always larger than covalent radii, group 18 elements have larger radii than group 17 elements.

Thus, group 17 elements possess the smallest atomic radii in their respective periods.

Answer: group 17

58235.text: Which of the following statements is false about oxygen and sulphur?
options: Atoms of oxygen and sulphur consist two unpaired electrons in valence shell.
Oxygen and sulphur show $-2,+4$ and +6 oxidation states.
Oxygen is gas while sulphur is solid at room temperature.
Hydride of oxygen is more stable than hydride of sulphur.
58235.sol:
To identify the false statement, each option is evaluated against the chemical properties of oxygen and sulphur.

A) Both oxygen ($[\text{He}] 2s^2 2p^4$) and sulphur ($[\text{Ne}] 3s^2 3p^4$) possess two unpaired electrons in their valence p-orbitals. This statement is true.

B) Oxygen rarely exhibits oxidation states beyond $+2$ due to high electronegativity and lack of d-orbitals, whereas sulphur commonly shows $+4$ and $+6$ states. Oxygen does not demonstrate $+4$ or $+6$ oxidation states, making this statement false.

C) At room temperature, oxygen exists as a diatomic gas ($\text{O}_2$), and sulphur is a solid ($\text{S}_8$). This statement is true.

D) The bond dissociation enthalpy of $\text{O–H}$ in $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is greater than that of $\text{S–H}$ in $\text{H}_2\text{S}$, resulting in higher thermal stability for $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. This statement is true.

The false statement is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

60216.text: The co-ordinates of the point on the curve $y = x\log x$ at which the normal is parallel to the line $2x - 2y = 3$ are...
60216.sol:
Given curve is $y = x \log x$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \log x + x \cdot \dfrac{1}{x} = \log x + 1$

The normal to the curve is parallel to the line $2x - 2y = 3$, which has a slope of $1$.

Since the normal is perpendicular to the tangent, the slope of the tangent is $-1$.

Equating the derivative to the slope of the tangent:

$\log x + 1 = -1$

$\log x = -2$

$x = e^{-2}$

Substituting $x = e^{-2}$ in the equation of the curve:

$y = e^{-2} \log(e^{-2}) = -2e^{-2}$

The required point is $(e^{-2}, -2e^{-2})$.

Answer: $(e^{-2}, -2e^{-2})$

60281.text: 20 is divided into two parts so that the product of the cube of one part and the square of the other part is maximum, then these two parts are
60281.sol:
Let the two parts be $x$ and $y$ such that $x + y = 20$ and $P = x^3 y^2$. Expressing $y = 20 - x$ gives $P(x) = x^3 (20 - x)^2$.

Differentiate using the product rule: $P'(x) = 3x^2 (20 - x)^2 - 2x^3 (20 - x) = x^2(20 - x)(60 - 5x)$.

Set $P'(x) = 0$ to find critical points: $x = 0$, $x = 20$, or $x = 12$. The endpoints $x = 0$ and $x = 20$ yield $P = 0$, while $x = 12$ gives $y = 8$ and $P = 12^3 \times 8^2 = 110592$.

The derivative changes from positive to negative at $x = 12$, confirming a maximum. Among the options, $C$ corresponds to $12$ and $8$ with the highest product.

Answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

The series becomes $\binom{16}{5}+\binom{16}{6}+\binom{17}{7}+\binom{18}{8}$

$\binom{16}{5}+\binom{16}{6}=\binom{17}{6}$
$\binom{17}{6}+\binom{17}{7}=\binom{18}{7}$

The expression simplifies to $\binom{18}{7}+\binom{18}{8}=\binom{19}{8}$

Thus $\binom{19}{8}=\binom{19}{r}$

This equality holds when $r=8$ or $r=19-8=11$

The solution corresponds to option D.

62537.subject: Mathematics
62537.text: The value of $\cot^{-1} \left[\dfrac{\sqrt{1 - \sin x} + \sqrt{1 + \sin x}}{\sqrt{1 - \sin x} - \sqrt{1 + \sin x}}\right], where $x \in  $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ is...
62537.sol:
We know that $1 \pm \sin x = \left(\cos \dfrac{x}{2} \pm \sin \dfrac{x}{2}\right)^2$.

Since $x \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, we have $\dfrac{x}{2} \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$.

In this interval, $\cos \dfrac{x}{2} > \sin \dfrac{x}{2} > 0$.

Therefore, $\sqrt{1 - \sin x} = \cos \dfrac{x}{2} - \sin \dfrac{x}{2}$ and $\sqrt{1 + \sin x} = \cos \dfrac{x}{2} + \sin \dfrac{x}{2}$.

Substituting these values into the given expression:

$\dfrac{\sqrt{1 - \sin x} + \sqrt{1 + \sin x}}{\sqrt{1 - \sin x} - \sqrt{1 + \sin x}} = \dfrac{\left(\cos \dfrac{x}{2} - \sin \dfrac{x}{2}\right) + \left(\cos \dfrac{x}{2} + \sin \dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{\left(\cos \dfrac{x}{2} - \sin \dfrac{x}{2}\right) - \left(\cos \dfrac{x}{2} + \sin \dfrac{x}{2}\right)}$

$= \dfrac{2\cos \dfrac{x}{2}}{-2\sin \dfrac{x}{2}} = -\cot \dfrac{x}{2}$

The given expression becomes $\cot^{-1}\left(-\cot \dfrac{x}{2}\right)$.

Using the property $\cot^{-1}(-y) = \pi - \cot^{-1}y$:

$\cot^{-1}\left(-\cot \dfrac{x}{2}\right) = \pi - \cot^{-1}\left(\cot \dfrac{x}{2}\right)$

Since $\dfrac{x}{2} \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$, $\cot^{-1}\left(\cot \dfrac{x}{2}\right) = \dfrac{x}{2}$.

Thus, the value is $\pi - \dfrac{x}{2}$.

Answer: $\pi - \dfrac{x}{2}$

63187.text: If matrix $A=\frac{1}{11}\left[\begin{array}{rrr}-1 & 7 & -24 \\ 2 & a & 4 \\ 2 & -3 & 15\end{array}\right]$ and $A^{-1}=\left[\begin{array}{rrr}3 & 3 & 4 \\ 2 & -3 & 4 \\ b & -1 & c\end{array}\right]$, then the values of $a, b, c$ respectively are ......
63187.sol:
Given the matrices:

$A = \frac{1}{11}\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 7 & -24 \\ 2 & a & 4 \\ 2 & -3 & 15\end{bmatrix}$

$A^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix}3 & 3 & 4 \\ 2 & -3 & 4 \\ b & -1 & c\end{bmatrix}$

Since $A \times A^{-1} = I$, we compute the product without the scalar factor first:

$\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 7 & -24 \\ 2 & a & 4 \\ 2 & -3 & 15\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}3 & 3 & 4 \\ 2 & -3 & 4 \\ b & -1 & c\end{bmatrix} = 11I$

Determine $b$ from the (1,1) entry:

$(-1)(3) + (7)(2) + (-24)(b) = 11 \Rightarrow -3 + 14 - 24b = 11 \Rightarrow -24b = 0 \Rightarrow b = 0$

Determine $a$ from the (2,2) entry:

$(2)(3) + (a)(-3) + (4)(-1) = 11 \Rightarrow 6 - 3a - 4 = 11 \Rightarrow -3a = 9 \Rightarrow a = -3$

Determine $c$ from the (3,3) entry:

$(2)(4) + (-3)(4) + (15)(c) = 11 \Rightarrow 8 - 12 + 15c = 11 \Rightarrow 15c = 15 \Rightarrow c = 1$

Verification confirms all non-diagonal entries yield $0$ as required.
The values are $a = -3$, $b = 0$, $c = 1$, corresponding to option C.

63498.subject: Mathematics
63498.text: If four digit numbers are formed by using the digits $1,2,3,4,5,6,7$ without repetition, then out of these numbers, the numbers exactly divisible by 25 are
63498.sol:
For a four-digit number formed from the digits $\{1,2,3,4,5,6,7\}$ to be divisible by 25, its last two digits must form a number divisible by 25.

The possible two-digit endings are $25$ and $75$, as $00$ and $50$ are not feasible without the digit $0$.

Case ending in 25: The digits 2 and 5 are used, leaving $\{1,3,4,6,7\}$ for the first two positions. There are $5 \times 4 = 20$ arrangements.

Case ending in 75: The digits 7 and 5 are used, leaving $\{1,2,3,4,6\}$ for the first two positions. There are $5 \times 4 = 20$ arrangements.

Total numbers: $20 + 20 = 40$.

The number of valid four-digit numbers divisible by 25 is $\boxed{40}$.

64377.subject: Mathematics
64377.text: If the lines $2x = ky = -z$ and $6x = -y = -4z$ are perpendicular to each other then the value of $k$ is...
64377.sol:
The equations of the given lines can be rewritten in standard symmetric form as:

$\dfrac{x}{1/2} = \dfrac{y}{1/k} = \dfrac{z}{-1}$

$\dfrac{x}{1/6} = \dfrac{y}{-1} = \dfrac{z}{-1/4}$

The direction ratios of the first line are $a_1 = \dfrac{1}{2}$, $b_1 = \dfrac{1}{k}$, $c_1 = -1$.

The direction ratios of the second line are $a_2 = \dfrac{1}{6}$, $b_2 = -1$, $c_2 = -\dfrac{1}{4}$.

Since the two lines are perpendicular to each other, the sum of the products of their corresponding direction ratios must be zero:

$a_1 a_2 + b_1 b_2 + c_1 c_2 = 0$

$\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{6}\right) + \left(\dfrac{1}{k}\right)(-1) + (-1)\left(-\dfrac{1}{4}\right) = 0$

$\dfrac{1}{12} - \dfrac{1}{k} + \dfrac{1}{4} = 0$

$\dfrac{1}{k} = \dfrac{1}{12} + \dfrac{3}{12}$

$\dfrac{1}{k} = \dfrac{4}{12}$

$\dfrac{1}{k} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$k = 3$

Answer: $3$

66066.text: A parallel plate air capacitor has capacity ' $C$ ' and distance of separation between plates is ' d '. If a conducting sheet of thickness $\frac{2 \mathrm{ d}}{3}$ is inserted in between the plates, the capacitance becomes $C_1$. The ratio of $\frac{C_1}{C}$ is
66066.sol:
The original capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor is $C = \frac{\epsilon_0 A}{d}$.

When a conducting sheet of thickness $t = \frac{2d}{3}$ is inserted, the electric field only exists in the air gaps. The effective separation becomes $d' = d - t = d - \frac{2d}{3} = \frac{d}{3}$.

The new capacitance is therefore $C_1 = \frac{\epsilon_0 A}{d'} = \frac{\epsilon_0 A}{d/3} = \frac{3\epsilon_0 A}{d}$.

The ratio evaluates to $\frac{C_1}{C} = \frac{\frac{3\epsilon_0 A}{d}}{\frac{\epsilon_0 A}{d}} = 3$.

Final ratio: $\boxed{3}$

66336.text: The value of the shunt resistance that allows $10 \%$ of the main current through the galvanometer of $99 \Omega$ is
66336.sol:
The galvanometer with resistance $G = 99\,\Omega$ carries $I_g = 0.10 I$ of the main current $I$. The shunt resistance $S$ carries the remaining current $I_s = 0.90 I$.

Since the galvanometer and shunt are in parallel, the voltage across both must be equal:

$I_g G = I_s S$

Substituting the current expressions:

$(0.10 I) G = (0.90 I) S$

Canceling $I$ and solving for $S$:

$S = \frac{0.10}{0.90} G = \frac{1}{9} \times 99 = 11\,\Omega$

The shunt resistance required is $11\,\Omega$, corresponding to option B.

70407.subject: Physics
70407.text: The equation of a progressive wave is given by $y = 6\cos(100t - 4x)$ where $y$ is in $\mu\text{m}$, $x$ in metre and $t$ in second. The ratio of the maximum particle velocity to the velocity of wave is
70407.sol:
The given equation of the progressive wave is $y = 6\cos(100t - 4x)$.

Comparing this with the standard wave equation $y = A\cos(\omega t - kx)$, we get:
Amplitude $A = 6 \mu\text{m} = 6 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$
Angular frequency $\omega = 100 \text{ rad/s}$
Wave number $k = 4 \text{ m}^{-1}$

The maximum particle velocity is given by $v_{p,\text\max} = A\omega$.

The velocity of the wave is given by $v_w = \dfrac{\omega}{k}$.

The ratio of the maximum particle velocity to the wave velocity is:
$\dfrac{v_{p,\text\max}}{v_w} = \dfrac{A\omega}{\dfrac{\omega}{k}} = Ak$

Substituting the values of $A$ and $k$:
$\text{Ratio} = (6 \times 10^{-6}) \times 4 = 24 \times 10^{-6} = 2.4 \times 10^{-5}$

Answer: $2.4 \times 10^{-5}$

71307.subject: Biology
71307.text: Accelerated pace of growth is observed in plants during __________.
71307.sol:
The growth of a plant organ is generally divided into three phases: cell division (meristematic), cell elongation, and cell maturation.

During the cell division phase, the rate of growth is relatively slow, representing the lag phase of the growth curve.

During the cell elongation phase, cells undergo rapid enlargement, increased vacuolation, and new cell wall deposition. This corresponds to the log or exponential phase of the sigmoid growth curve, where an accelerated pace of growth is observed.

During the cell maturation phase, the growth rate slows down as cells attain their maximal size and undergo differentiation, representing the stationary phase.

Answer: cell elongation

71447.subject: Biology
71447.text: Which enzyme is responsible for phosphorylation of glucose with ATP?
71447.sol:
The first step of glycolysis involves the phosphorylation of glucose to form glucose-6-phosphate.

This reaction is catalyzed by the enzyme hexokinase, which uses ATP as the phosphate donor.

Phosphofructokinase catalyzes the phosphorylation of fructose-6-phosphate to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate.

Aldolase catalyzes the cleavage of fructose-1,6-bisphosphate into two three-carbon sugars.

Phosphohexose isomerase catalyzes the isomerization of glucose-6-phosphate to fructose-6-phosphate.

Answer: Hexokinase

71475.subject: Biology
71475.text: Which one of the following is NOT an outbreeding device to promote cross pollination?
71475.sol:
Outbreeding devices are mechanisms developed by plants to prevent self-pollination and promote cross-pollination.

Herkogamy is the presence of a physical barrier between the anther and stigma, which prevents self-pollination.

Self-sterility or self-incompatibility is a genetic mechanism that prevents self-pollen from fertilizing the ovules of the same flower.

Heteromorphy involves the production of flowers with different lengths of styles and stamens, which promotes cross-pollination.

Cleistogamy refers to the condition where flowers never open, ensuring strict self-pollination and completely preventing cross-pollination. Thus, it is an inbreeding device, not an outbreeding device.

Answer: Cleistogamy

71493.subject: Biology
71493.text: Identify the correct ratio of microspore mother cells, vegetative cells, generative cells and male gametes produced in a microsporangium, if 40 pollen grains are released from it.
71493.sol:
One microspore mother cell (MMC) undergoes meiosis to produce $4$ microspores, which develop into $4$ pollen grains.

Number of MMCs required to produce $40$ pollen grains = $\dfrac{40}{4} = 10$.

Each pollen grain contains $1$ vegetative cell and $1$ generative cell.

Number of vegetative cells in $40$ pollen grains = $40$.

Number of generative cells in $40$ pollen grains = $40$.

Each generative cell divides to form $2$ male gametes.

Number of male gametes produced = $40 \times 2 = 80$.

The ratio of microspore mother cells : vegetative cells : generative cells : male gametes is $10 : 40 : 40 : 80$, which simplifies to $1 : 4 : 4 : 8$.

Answer: $1:4:4:8$

72278.subject: Physics
72278.text: For the vector $\vec{A}$ making an angle $\theta$ with the negative X-axis and lying in the third quadrant, the standard resolved form is
72278.sol:
The vector $\vec{A}$ lies in the third quadrant and makes an angle $\theta$ with the negative X-axis.

The component of the vector along the negative X-axis is $A\cos\theta$, so $A_x = -A\cos\theta$.

The component of the vector along the negative Y-axis is $A\sin\theta$, so $A_y = -A\sin\theta$.

Therefore, the vector in standard resolved form is $\vec{A} = -A\cos\theta\,\hat{i} - A\sin\theta\,\hat{j}$.

Answer: $-A\cos\theta\,\hat{i} - A\sin\theta\,\hat{j}$

72317.subject: Physics
72317.text: Two SHM's $x_1 = a\sin \left(\omega$ t + $\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$ and $ x_2 = a\sin($\omega$ t + \pi) are superimposed on each other. The resultant amplitude of motion is $(\sin $\pi$/2 = 1$ and \cos \pi$/2 = 0)$$
72317.sol:
Given equations of SHM are $x_1 = a\sin \left(\omega$ t + $\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$ and $ x_2 = a\sin($\omega$ t + \pi).

The phase difference between the two SHMs is \Delta\phi = \dfrac{3\pi}{2} - \pi = \dfrac{\pi}{2}.

The resultant amplitude $ A$ is given by A = \sqrt{a_1^2 + a_2^2 + 2a_1a_2\cos(\Delta\phi)}.

Substituting $ a_1 = a$, $a_2 = a$, and \Delta\phi = \dfrac{\pi}{2}:

$ A = $\sqrt{a^2 + a^2 + 2a^2\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}

Since \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) =0$, we get:

A = \sqrt{2a^2} = a\sqrt{2}$$

Answer: $$a\sqrt{2}

77464.text:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let the function $y = (1 - \cos x)^{-1}$, where $x \neq 2n\pi$ and $n$ is an integer.

What is $\int y \, dx$ equal to?
77464.sol:
Given $y = (1 - \cos x)^{-1}$

$y = \dfrac{1}{1 - \cos x}$

Using the half-angle formula $1 - \cos x = 2 \sin^2(x/2)$

$y = \dfrac{1}{2 \sin^2(x/2)} = \dfrac{1}{2} \csc^2(x/2)$

Integrating with respect to $x$:

$\int y \, dx = \int \dfrac{1}{2} \csc^2(x/2) \, dx$

$\int y \, dx = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \dfrac{-\cot(x/2)}{1/2} \right) + c$

$\int y \, dx = -\cot(x/2) + c$

Answer: $-\cot(x/2) + c$

77693.subject: Mathematics
77693.text: If $M_k=\begin{bmatrix} k & k-1 \\ k-1 & k \end{bmatrix}$ where $k$ is a natural number, then what is $|M_1|+|M_2|+|M_3|+\ldots+|M_{50}|$ equal to ?
77693.sol:
Given $M_k = \begin{bmatrix} k & k-1 \\ k-1 & k \end{bmatrix}$

The determinant of $M_k$ is given by:

$|M_k| = k^2 - (k-1)^2$

$|M_k| = k^2 - (k^2 - 2k + 1) = 2k - 1$

The required sum is:

$|M_1| + |M_2| + |M_3| + \ldots + |M_{50}| = \sum_{k=1}^{50} (2k - 1)$

This represents the sum of the first $50$ odd natural numbers, which forms an arithmetic progression:

$1 + 3 + 5 + \ldots + 99$

The sum of an arithmetic progression is given by $\dfrac{n}{2}(a + l)$, where $n = 50$, $a = 1$, and $l = 99$:

Sum $= \dfrac{50}{2} (1 + 99) = 25 \times 100 = 2500$

Answer: $2500$

77971.subject: Mathematics
77971.text:
Passage: Four dice are rolled.

Question: What is the probability that getting a total of the numbers on the dice is $6$ ?
77971.sol:
Total number of outcomes when four dice are rolled is $6^4 = 1296$.

Let $x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4$ be the numbers appearing on the four dice. We need to find the number of solutions to the equation:

$x_1 + x_2 + x_3 + x_4 = 6$

where $1 \le x_i \le 6$ for $i = 1, 2, 3, 4$.

Let $x_i = y_i + 1$, where $y_i \ge 0$. Substituting this into the equation, we get:

$(y_1 + 1) + (y_2 + 1) + (y_3 + 1) + (y_4 + 1) = 6$

$y_1 + y_2 + y_3 + y_4 = 2$

The number of non-negative integer solutions to this equation is given by ^{n+r-1}C_{r-1}$, where $n=2$ and $r=4$.

Number of favorable outcomes = ^{2+4-1}C_{4-1} = ^{5}C_{3} = 10$.

The required probability is $\dfrac{10}{1296} = \dfrac{5}{648}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{5}{648}$

78352.subject: Mathematics
78352.text: What is the harmonic mean of the numbers $C(10,3)$, $C(10,4)$, $C(10,5)$, $C(10,6)$ and $C(10,7)$?
78352.sol:
The given numbers are $^{10}C_{3}$, $^{10}C_{4}$, $^{10}C_{5}$, $^{10}C_{6}$, and $^{10}C_{7}$.

Calculating their values:
$^{10}C_{3} = \dfrac{10 \times 9 \times 8}{3 \times 2 \times 1} = 120$
$^{10}C_{4} = \dfrac{10 \times 9 \times 8 \times 7}{4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1} = 210$
$^{10}C_{5} = \dfrac{10 \times 9 \times 8 \times 7 \times 6}{5 \times 4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1} = 252$
$^{10}C_{6} = ^{10}C_{4} = 210$
$^{10}C_{7} = ^{10}C_{3} = 120$

The harmonic mean $H$ of $n$ numbers $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n$ is given by:
$H = \dfrac{n}{\dfrac{1}{x_1} + \dfrac{1}{x_2} + \dots + \dfrac{1}{x_n}}$

Here $n = 5$. The sum of the reciprocals is:
$S = \dfrac{1}{120} + \dfrac{1}{210} + \dfrac{1}{252} + \dfrac{1}{210} + \dfrac{1}{120}$

$S = \dfrac{2}{120} + \dfrac{2}{210} + \dfrac{1}{252}$

$S = \dfrac{1}{60} + \dfrac{1}{105} + \dfrac{1}{252}$

Taking the LCM of $60, 105, 252$, which is $1260$:
$S = \dfrac{21 + 12 + 5}{1260} = \dfrac{38}{1260} = \dfrac{19}{630}$

The harmonic mean is:
$H = \dfrac{5}{S} = \dfrac{5}{\dfrac{19}{630}} = \dfrac{3150}{19}$

Answer: $3150/19$

78374.subject: Mathematics
78374.text:
Paragraph: Let $P$ be the sum of first $n$ positive terms of an increasing arithmetic progression $A$. Let $Q$ be the sum of first $n$ positive terms of another increasing arithmetic progression $B$. Let $P: Q=(5 n+4):(9 n+6)$
Question: If $d$ is the common difference of $A$, and $D$ is the common difference of $B$, then which one of the following is always correct?
78374.sol:
There are two AP with the different first terms and common difference.
For the first AP A:
Let the first term be a and common difference $=\mathrm{d}$
Sum of n terms $\mathrm{P}=\frac{n}{2}[2 a+(n-1) d]
and \mathrmn^{\text{th }}$ term $a_n=a+(n-1) d$
For the second AP B:
Let the first term be M and common difference $=\mathrm{D}$
Sum of n terms $\mathrm{Q}=\frac{n}{2}[2 M+(n-1) D]
and n^{\text{th }}$ term $M_n=M+(n-1) D$
It is given that
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\text{ Sum$ of $} n \text{ terms of first A.P }}{\text{ Sum of } n \text{ terms of second A.P }}=\frac{5 n+4}{9 n+6} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\frac{n}{2}[2 a+(n-1) d]}{\frac{n}{2}[2 M+(n-1) D]}=\frac{5 n+4}{9 n+6} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{[2 a+(n-1) d]}{[2 M+(n-1) D]}=\frac{5 n+4}{9 n+6} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{a+\left(\frac{n-1}{2}\right) d}{M+\left(\frac{n-1}{2}\right) D}=\frac{5 n+4}{9 n+6} \ldots . . \text{ (1) }
\end{aligned}$
Now, we need to find the ratio of the first term of A and $B\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1^{\text{st }} \text{ term$ of $} A}{1^{\text{st }} \text{ term of } B} \\
& =\frac{a}{M}
\end{aligned}$
Hence, $\frac{n-1}{2}=0 \Rightarrow n=1$
Putting $\mathrm{n}=1$ in equation (1), we get
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{a}{M}=\frac{5(1)+4}{9(1)+6} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{a}{M}=\frac{9}{15} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{a}{M}=\frac{3}{5} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{1^{\text{st }} \text{ term of } A}{1^{\text{st }} \text{ term of } B}=\frac{3}{5}
\end{aligned}$
Now, we need to find the ratio of the second term of $A and B\begin{aligned}
& \frac{2^{\text{nd }} \text{ term of } A}{2^{\text{nd }} t \text{ erm of } B} \\
& =\frac{a+(2-1) d}{M+(2-1) D} \\
& =\frac{a+d}{M+D}
\end{aligned}$
Hence, $\frac{n-1}{2}=1 \Rightarrow n=3$
Putting $\mathrm{n}=3$ in equation (1), we get
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{a+d}{M+D}=\frac{5(3)+4}{9(3)+6} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{a+d}{M+D}=\frac{19}{33} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{2^{\text{nd }} \text{ term of } A}{2^{\text{nd }} \text{ term of } B}=\frac{19}{33}
\end{aligned}$
Let the first term of $A=3$ and the second term of $A=19$ then common difference $d=19-3=16$
Let the first term of $B=5$ and the second term of $B=33$ then common difference $D=33-5=28$
Hence, $D > d\therefore$ The correct option is (1)

78518.subject: Mathematics
78518.text:
Passage: The frequency distribution of marks obtained by $100$ students in a certain subject is given below :
Marks$0$-$10$$10$-$20$$20$-$30$$30$-$40$
No. of students$10$$20$$f$$40$


Question: What is the mean deviation about the arithmetic mean ?
78518.sol:
Total number of students is $100$.

$10 + 20 + f + 40 = 100 \Rightarrow f = 30$

The mid-points $x_i$ of the classes are $5, 15, 25, 35$.

The arithmetic mean $\bar{x} = \dfrac{\sum f_i x_i}{\sum f_i}$

$\bar{x} = \dfrac{10 \times 5 + 20 \times 15 + 30 \times 25 + 40 \times 35}{100}$

$\bar{x} = \dfrac{50 + 300 + 750 + 1400}{100} = \dfrac{2500}{100} = 25$

The absolute deviations $|x_i - \bar{x}|$ are $|5 - 25| = 20$, $|15 - 25| = 10$, $|25 - 25| = 0$, and $|35 - 25| = 10$.

Mean deviation about the mean $= \dfrac{\sum f_i |x_i - \bar{x}|}{\sum f_i}$

$= \dfrac{10 \times 20 + 20 \times 10 + 30 \times 0 + 40 \times 10}{100}$

$= \dfrac{200 + 200 + 0 + 400}{100} = \dfrac{800}{100} = 8$

Answer: $8$

81565.subject: Chemistry
81565.text:
The number of chlorine atoms present in the organic products X and Y of the following reactions, respectively, are :
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + 6\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow[\text{dark, cold}]{\text{Anhydr. AlCl}_3} X$
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + 3\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow[500\ \text{K}]{\text{UV}} Y$
81565.sol:
Reaction 1 is an electrophilic aromatic substitution. Benzene reacts with excess chlorine in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ (a Lewis acid) to form hexachlorobenzene ($\text{C}_6\text{Cl}_6$).

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + 6\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow[\text{dark, cold}]{\text{Anhydr. AlCl}_3} \text{C}_6\text{Cl}_6 + 6\text{HCl}$

The organic product X is hexachlorobenzene, which contains $6$ chlorine atoms.

Reaction 2 is a free radical addition reaction. Benzene reacts with chlorine in the presence of UV light to form benzene hexachloride ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_6\text{Cl}_6$), also known as gammaxene or lindane.

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + 3\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow[500\ \text{K}]{\text{UV}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_6\text{Cl}_6$

The organic product Y is benzene hexachloride, which contains $6$ chlorine atoms.

Therefore, the number of chlorine atoms in both X and Y is $6$.

Answer: $6$ and $6$

The $t$ RNA molecule has a distinctive folded structure with three hairpin loops that form the shape of a threeleafed clover. options: establishes sites of the genes on a chromosomes

shows the distribution of various species in a region
84989.sol:
A genetic map is a type of chromosome map that shows the relative locations of genes and other important features. The map is based on the idea of linkage, which means that the closer two genes are to each other on the chromosome, the greater the probability that they will be inherited together.
Related Theory
In genetics, a centimorgan (cM) or map unit (m.u.) is a unit for measuring genetic linkage. It is defined as the distance between chromosome positions (also termed loci or markers) for which the expected average number of intervening chromosomal crossovers in a single generation is 0.01.

87693.text: ${}_{84}Po^{210}$ decays with a particle to ${}_{82}Pb^{206}$ with a half-life of 138.4 days. If 1.0 g of ${}_{84}Po^{210}$ is placed in a sealed tube, how much helium will accumulate in 69.2 days. Express the answer in $cm^{3}$ at STP.
87693.sol:
${t}_{1 / 2} = 138.4$ days, t = 69.2 day

Number of half-lifes $n = \dfrac{t}{{t}_{1 / 2}} = \dfrac{69.2}{138.4} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Amount of Po left $\dfrac{1}{2}$ after half-life $= \dfrac{1}{{\left(2\right)}^{1 / 2}}g = 0.707g$

Amount of Po used in $\dfrac{1}{2}$ half-life $= 1 - 0.707 = 0.293g$

Now $84Po^{210} \to 82Pb^{206} + 2{He}^{4}$

210 g Po on decay will produce = 4g He

0.293 g Po on decay will produce $= \dfrac{4 \times 0.293}{210} = 5.581 \times {10}^{- 3}gHe$

Volume of He at STP $= \dfrac{5.581 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 22400}{4} = 31.25mL = 31.25cm^{3}$

90296.text: Consider the function $f\left(x\right) = \left(x - 2\right)\left|x^{2} - 3x + 2\right|$, then the incorrect statement is
90296.sol:
$∵ x - 2 \text{ and } \left|{x}^{2} - 3x + 2\right|$ both are continuous $∀ x \in R$

Now, $\left|{x}^{2} - 3x + 2\right| = \left|\left(x - 1\right)\left(x - 2\right)\right|$

$f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}\left(x - 1\right){\left(x - 2\right)}^{2} & : & x \in \left(- \infty, 1\right) ∪ \left(2, \infty\right) \\ - \left(x - 1\right){\left(x - 2\right)}^{2} & : & x \in \left[1,2\right]\end{cases}\right)

Clearly, ${f}^{′} \left({2}^{-}\right) = f\text{'}\left({2}^{+}\right) = 0 ⇒ f\left(x\right)$ is differentiable at $x = 2$

Hence, \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \sec^{2}$⁡ x + cos ⁡ x$

93377.text: A small spherical ball (obeying Stoke's law for viscous force) is thrown up vertically with a speed $20m{s}^{- 1}$ and is received back by the thrower at the point of projection with a speed $10m{s}^{- 1}$. Neglecting the buoyant force on the ball, assuming the speed of the ball during its flight to be never equal to its terminal speed and taking the acceleration due to gravity $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$, find the time of flight of the ball in seconds.
93377.sol:
$m\overset{\to}{g} + k\overset{\to}{v} = \dfrac{md\overset{\to}{v}}{dt}$

$\overset{\to}{g}dt + \dfrac{k}{m}\overset{\to}{v}dt = d\overset{\to}{v}$

Integrating both sides ${∫}_{0}^{T}\overset{\to}{g}dt + \dfrac{k}{m}{∫}_{0}^{T}\overset{\to}{v}dt = ∫ \overset{\to}{u}\overset{\to}{v}d\overset{\to}{v}$

$\overset{\to}{g}T + 0 = \overset{\to}{v} - \overset{\to}{u}$

$gT = v - \left(- u\right) = v + u$

$⇒ T = \dfrac{v + u}{g} = 3s$

95193.sol:
There are four types of primary xylem development:& exarch, endarch, centrarch, and mesarch.
In& endarch& development, the protoxylem begins its development from the innermost procambial cells located adjacent to the pith and development progresses outward. 95388.subject: Botany
95388.text: Metagenesis or alteration of generation can be observed in members of phylum
95388.sol:
Metagenesis (or alternation of generation) Coelenterates exhibit two body forms: polyp and medusa.

A. Polyp = Sessile and cylindrical like Hydra, Adamsia.

B. Medusa = Free swimming, umbrella shaped like Aurelia (jelly fish). Those cnidarians in which both polyp and medusa alternates with each other, are said to exhibit metagenesis. During metagenesis, polyp (asexual stage) reproduce asexually to form medusa, whereas the medusa (sexual stage) sexually reproduce to form polyp, e.g., Obelia.

96054.subject: Botany
96054.text: Glycolipids in the plasma membrane are located at
options: Inner leaflet of the plasma membrane
The outer leaflet of the plasma membrane
Evenly distributed in the inner and outer leaflets
It varies according to cell types
96054.sol: In eukaryotes, the cell membrane is explained as a fluid mosaic model by Schleiden and Schwann. According to this model the plasma membrane is made up of lipids and proteins. The lipids are arranged in a bilayer. The lipids present are phospholipids. These are arranged in such a way that the polar heads are towards the outer side and hydrophobic ends are towards the inner side. The ratio of proteins and lipids are different in different cell types. In humans it is seen that around 40 percent is lipid and 52 percent is protein. This explains that the quasi- fluid nature of lipid causes the movement of proteins throughout the bilayer structure. The glycolipids are oriented towards outside the plasma membrane and are extrinsic in nature.

96168.text: Two features present in meiosis but absent in mitosis are
options: Pairing of homologous chromosomes and recombination between them
96168.sol: Homologous chromosomes are made up of chromosome pairs of approximately the same length, centromere position, and staining pattern, for genes with the same corresponding loci. One homologous chromosome is inherited from the organism's mother; the other is inherited from the organism's father. They have a tendency to pair with each other during meiosis and undergoes crossing over to produce new genetic recombinations.

96212.sol: The stages of nuclear division in mitosis are prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase. Prophase is the longest phase of mitosis while anaphase is the shortest phase. Anaphase is characterized by splitting of centromere and pulling of chromosomes towards the poles.

96425.text: Which kind of pyramid will be obtained if& a small standing crop of lower trophic levels supports large standing crop of higher trophic levels?
96425.sol: Each trophic level has a certain mass of living material at a particular time called the standing crop. The standing crop is measured as the mass of living organisms (biomass) or the number in a unit area. When the lower levels have lower standing crop than the higher level, the pyramid will be inverted, as in the case of the pyramid of biomass in an aquatic ecosystem.

96809.text: Pentamerous actinomorphic flowers, bicarpellary ovary with oblique septa, and fruit capsule or berry are characteristic features of family
96809.sol: A pentamerous actinomorphic flower is one where the floral parts are in multiples of five and the flower can be divided into two equal halves in more than one plane. The gynoecium is bicarpellary, syncarpous, forming a superior bilocular ovary. Each locule has many ovules on axile placentation. Members of Solanaceae are characterized by the presence of an obliquely placed septum in the ovary and highly swollen placentae. The oblique septum is probably due to shifting in the position of the ovary.

How many plants in the list given below have marginal placentation?

Mustard, Gram, Tulip, Asparagus, Arhar, Sun hemp, Chilli, Colchicum, Onion, Moong, Pea, Tobacco, Lupin
97070.sol:
Placentation is the arrangement of the ovules in the ovary and their attachment to it. Placentation are of various type in the angiosperms - marginal, axile, central, parietal, basal, and free central. In marginal placentation, ovules are attached to the ridge formed on the ventral suture of the ovary. It occurs in the monocarpellary and unilocular ovary.

Gram, Arhar, Sun Hemp, Moong, Lupin and Pea the marginal placentation.

Mustard has parietal placentation.

Axile placentation is shown by Tulip, Asparagus, Colchicium, chili, onion.

97278.text: Spraying of juvenile conifers with which hormone hastens the maturity period and thus leading to early seed production?
options: The hormone which also causes bolting in some plants
The hormone which is activated during deficiency of water
The hormone which is responsible for apical dominance
The hormone which prevents apical dominance is plants
97278.sol: The hormone which also causes bolting in some plants is Gibberellin. Gibberellins are growth promoters. They were first discovered in a fungus Gibberella fujikuroi. There are many gibberellins and they are denoted as GA1, GA2, GA3 and so on. However, GA3 was one of the first gibberellins to be discovered and remains the most intensively studied form. Spraying juvenile conifers with GAs hastens the maturity period, thus leading to early seed production. Gibberellins also promotes bolting (internode elongation just prior to flowering) in beet, cabbages and many plants with rosette habit.The hormone which is activated during deficiency of water is absicisic acid, the hormone which is responsible for apical dominance is auxin and the hormone which prevents apical dominance is plants is cytokinin.

100261.subject: Physics
100261.text:
Assertion : Particle A is moving eastwards and particle B northwards with same speed. Then, velocity of A with respect to \(B\) is in south-east direction.
Reason : Relative velocity between them is zero as their speeds are same.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
If both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
If Assertion is true but Reason is false
If Assertion is false but Reason is true
100261.sol:
Assertion is true: Let velocity of \(A\) be \($\mathrm{v}$\_A=v $\mathrm{i}$\) (eastwards) and velocity of \(B\) be \($\mathrm{v}$\_B=v $\mathrm{j}$\) (northwards), where \(v\) is the speed. The velocity of \(A\) with respect to \(B\) is \($\mathrm{v}$\_A B=$\mathrm{v}$\_A-$\mathrm{v}$\_B=v $\mathrm{i}$\) -vj . This vector has a positive x -component and a negative y -component, which corresponds to the south-east direction.
Reason is false: Relative velocity is zero only if both the magnitude and direction of the velocities are the same. Here, only the magnitudes (speeds) are the same, but their directions are perpendicular (east vs. north). Therefore, their relative velocity is not zero.

100535.text: The radii of circular paths of two particles of same mass are in ratio $6: 8$ then what will be velocities ratio if they have a constant centripetal force?
100535.sol:
$\begin{aligned}$& $\text{ Here, } \frac{r_1}{r_2}=\frac{6}{8}, \frac{m_1}{m_2}=$1 \\
& $\frac{F_1}{F_2}=$1 $\text{ or, }$F_1=F_2 \\
& $\text{$ or $} \frac{m_1 v_1^2}{r_1}=\frac{m_2 v_2^2}{r_2}$\\
& $\text{$ or $} \frac{v_1^2}{v_2^2}=\frac{r_1}{r_2} \times \frac{m_2}{m_1}=\frac{6}{8} \times$1=$\frac{3}{4}$\\
& \therefore $\frac{v_1}{v_2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}
\end{aligned}$

100904.subject: Physics
100904.text: An upward force acting on a body varies with its vertical displacement $y$. The force increases linearly from $0$ to $400$ N as the displacement increases from $y = 0$ to $y = 10$ m. If the total time taken for this displacement is $4$ s, the average power delivered by the force is :
100904.sol:
Work done by the force is given by the area under the Force-displacement graph.

Since the force increases linearly from $0$ to $400$ N over a displacement of $10$ m, the area represents a triangle.

$W = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$

$W = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 400 = 2000$ J.

Average power is the total work done divided by the total time taken.

$P_{avg} = \dfrac{W}{t} = \dfrac{2000}{4} = 500$ W.

Answer: $500$ W

102881.subject: Physics
102881.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When two charged conducting spheres of different radii are connected by a thin conducting wire, the smaller sphere has a stronger electric field at its surface.
Reason (R): For spherical conductors at the same potential, the surface charge density is inversely proportional to the radius.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
102881.sol:
When two conducting spheres are connected by a wire, charge flows until their electrostatic potentials become equal ($V_1 = V_2 = V$).

The potential of a sphere of radius $R$ is $V = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{q}{R}$.
The surface charge density is $\sigma = \dfrac{q}{4\pi R^2}$.
Thus, $V = \dfrac{\sigma R}{\epsilon_0}$, which means $\sigma = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 V}{R}$.
Since $V$ is constant, $\sigma \propto \dfrac{1}{R}$. This makes the Reason (R) true.

The electric field at the surface of a conductor is given by $E = \dfrac{\sigma}{\epsilon_0}$.
Since $\sigma \propto \dfrac{1}{R}$, it follows that $E \propto \dfrac{1}{R}$.
Therefore, the smaller sphere (smaller $R$) will have a larger surface charge density and consequently a stronger electric field at its surface. This makes the Assertion (A) true.

Since the dependence of the electric field on the radius is directly derived from the surface charge density's dependence on the radius, Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

103580.text: If the magnetic dipole moment of an atom of diamagnetic material, paramagnetic material and ferromagnetic material are denoted by $\mu_d$, $\mu_p$ and $\mu_f$ respectively, then
103580.sol: In diamagnetic substances in each pair of electrons, the spin of both the electrons are in opposite directions. Hence, the electrons of each pair completely cancel the magnetic moment of each other. Thus, the net magnetic moment of each atom of such substances is zero i.e., $\mu_d=0$. The property of paramagnetism is found in those substances whose atoms, or molecules have an excess of electrons spinning in same direction. Hence, atoms of paramagnetic substances have permanent magnetic moment ie, $\mu_p \neq 0$. The property of ferromagnetism is found in substances which acquire very strong magnetism when placed in an external magnetic field. Like the paramagnetic substances each atom of ferromagnetic substances also has a permanent magnetic moment i.e, $\mu_f \neq 0$.

103665.subject: Physics
103665.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the magnetic field $B$ at a distance $r$ from the axis of a long straight current-carrying conductor (where $R$ is the radius of the conductor).

List-IList-II
(A) Inside a solid cylinder ($r < R$)(I) $B = 0$
(B) Outside a solid cylinder ($r > R$)(II) $B \propto \dfrac{1}{r}$
(C) Inside a thin-walled hollow cylinder ($r < R$)(III) $B \propto r$
(D) Outside a thin-walled hollow cylinder ($r > R$)(IV) $B \propto \dfrac{1}{r^2}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
103665.sol:
According to Ampere's circuital law:

For a solid current-carrying cylinder of radius $R$:
Inside ($r < R$): $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I r}{2\pi R^2}$, which means $B \propto r$. So, (A) matches with (III).
Outside ($r > R$): $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}$, which means $B \propto \dfrac{1}{r}$. So, (B) matches with (II).

For a thin-walled hollow current-carrying cylinder of radius $R$:
Inside ($r < R$): The enclosed current is zero, so $B = 0$. So, (C) matches with (I).
Outside ($r > R$): The cylinder behaves like a line current, $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}$, which means $B \propto \dfrac{1}{r}$. So, (D) matches with (II).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
